subject: qyzsbfdc trace: honest risk of 19...Kxc6 is 0, build says 0.00-0.63 across seeds (recovery scatter); proposal: history-sticky recovery
body: Replayed qyzsbfdc (we were Black vs duck, lost in 52 plies) through the root build (pawn deductions on, no A1) with 4 seeds, hybrid, node-limited. Decision after 19.Rxc6 (Black to move, frame 38): the honest king-loss risk of 19...Kxc6 is zero. The only unseen White piece that could attack c6 is the light bishop, and it is pinned by history to {d1,c2,b3,e2,g4,h5}: it was forced onto d1 by the recapture at frame 31, White's three later moves were one unobserved move, Rc1 (needed for Rxc6) and Rxc6 itself, and a4/b5 are visible-empty from our pawns. The build priced Kxc6 at 0.18 / 0.00 / 0.23 / 0.63 across seeds and recaptured in 1 of 4 (two seeds repeat the game's Bb4, one plays b5). That spread is recovery scatter: particles rebuilt after the surprise Rxc6 put the bishop on d5/e4, squares the particle's own past excludes. Proposal for your lane: history-sticky recovery, i.e. when a particle must be repaired, keep every unseen piece on its previous square unless the new observation contradicts it, and move only what the evidence forces; a cheaper variant keeps the set of squares each unseen piece could have reached in one unobserved move since it was last pinned. If your A1 + deductions copy already keeps the bishop off d5/e4 here, a paired trace at frame 38 of qyzsbfdc would show it. Other findings from the same replay: the final blunder 26...Kb8 into the rook on the 8th rank is avoided 4/4 by the current build, and 17...Nc6 onto the open c-file (the rook came to c1 one move later, unseen) is repeated 3/4, risk 0, because the threat is two plies deep and no one-ply term sees it. Arena v10 by opponent so far: Apricot 13-0, TA Baseline P 4-0, baseline.py 2-0, TA Baseline A 5-5, TA Baseline S 1-5, duck 1-9. I am running a sweep that replays every v10 loss at its last three decisions through the current build to count avoidable fatal moves; results go into HANDOFF.
